headline: A 2022 law lets existing federally funded health centers use New Access Point grants to set up mobile units without also opening a permanent site.
what_it_does: Health centers that already get Health Resources & Services Administration Health Center Program grants can now use New Access Point grants to start a mobile unit. Before this law, they could use those grants for a mobile unit only if they also opened a permanent location. The change removes that requirement.

who_it_affects.group: Health centers that receive HRSA Health Center Program grants
who_it_affects.how: They can use New Access Point grant money to set up a mobile unit even if they do not open a permanent new site.
People in these areas may be able to get primary care through mobile units that health centers can now fund with these grants.

when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a specific effective date; the law was enacted on October 17, 2022.
